To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Twitter provides complementary information for app development, (2) Twitter is more suitable than app stores for collecting bug reports and feature requests, (3) Twitter provides more detailed bug reports than app stores, (4) Twitter provides more feature requests than app stores and (5) Twitter is more effective than app stores for bug triaging and bug fixing
Twitter provides complementary information for app developers.
Twitter is a valuable resource for mobile app development, and that it provides complementary information about mobile apps to app store mining.
In summary, our research is concerned with
1) the extraction of app-related tweets; 2) the analysis of app-related tweets to identify feature requests and bug reports.
how to leverage social media for mobile app development.

the analysis of the Twitter stream to support mobile app developers in the following ways: 1) to detect and classify feature requests, bug reports, and app reviews; 2) to identify and rank the most important features and bugs; and 3) to identify and track the evolution of features over time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Twitter is an important complementary source for app store mining.
app store reviews and Twitter posts complement each other and that both are important sources of information for app development.
Twitter can provide complementary feedback to app store reviews.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information on Twitter is complementary to the information available in the app stores, which is a promising result for app developers and app store analysts.
Twitter is not a substitute for the app stores but a complementary source of information.
Twitter can be used as an alternative source to app store reviews to support app development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social media platforms such as Twitter provide a complementary source of information that is not currently exploited by app developers and researchers.
Twitter can provide complementary data to support the development of mobile applications.
app developers should not ignore social media as an additional channel of user feedback.
